title: Differential TTL for Metrics & Request Logs with Legal-Hold Snapshotting and Evidence Reconciler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers require different retention windows for metrics, operational request logs, prompts/responses, and aggregated embeddings. Legal holds and compliance audits require on-demand immutable snapshots and a way to prove that purges occurred (or were blocked) according to policy. Current retention workstreams address per-route TTLs and evidence exports, but we lack a coordinated approach for differential TTL across telemetry types with an automated evidence reconciler that can detect purge anomalies and produce signed proof bundles for auditors.

Goal: Design and deliver a retention assertor that: (1) applies per-tenant and per-artifact-type TTLs (metrics, logs, prompts/responses, embeddings), (2) supports legal-hold overrides and time-limited exemptions, (3) creates incremental cryptographic snapshot manifests before purges, and (4) exposes an evidence reconciler job that verifies purge completion, flags mismatches, and emits an attested export for compliance teams.

Scope: Prototype and productionize the orchestrator for hosted + dedicated modes; provide an opt-in private deployment recipe. Include console UI to view scheduled purges, holds, and reconciliation status. Integrate with existing evidence export API and audit timeline endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: System enforces independent TTLs for metrics, request-logs, prompts/responses, and embeddings per tenant and per route.
Legal-hold API allows creation/removal of holds with metadata (owner, justification, expiration) and prevents scheduled purges while active.
Before any purge, system generates an incremental snapshot manifest with content digests and a signed root hash stored in immutable object store.

Reconciler job verifies that objects scheduled for deletion are no longer accessible and produces an attested evidence bundle (manifest + verification log + proof chain) within 24 hours of a purge run.
Console UI shows upcoming purge windows, active holds, reconciler run results, and links to exported evidence bundles.
Automated alerts are raised when reconciler finds discrepancies (missing snapshot, failed deletion, or unexpected object retention) with severity mapping to customer_impact.
Works for hosted API customers and Dedicated pool tenants with documentation for Private deployment configuration.
Performance: reconciler job for a mid-size tenant (10B tokens/month) completes verification for a 30-day purge window within 2 hours in normal operating conditions.
Security review signed off and cryptographic primitives recorded in compliance artifact repository.
comments: 2025-11-10 — Aisha Patel: Initial triage. Captured gap between per-route TTL work and audit-grade evidence exports. Raised need for reconciler and legal-hold semantics.

2025-11-13 — Miguel Torres (ENG): Engineering notes: major design choices — snapshot-before-purge (immutable manifests) vs tombstone-indexing. Snapshot approach preferred for simpler forensic exports but adds storage overhead. Estimating ~5-10% additional storage depending on sampling strategy.

2025-11-18 — Design review (R&D): Recommended minimal UI surfaces: hold creation modal, purge schedule timeline, reconciler run history. Figma links attached in attachments. Need microcopy for legal justification field.

2025-11-22 — Security review kickoff (Priya Nair): Threat model added for evidence forgery and key rotation. Decision: use KMS-backed signing keys with rotation policy and append-only manifest store. Security review required: true.

2025-11-27 — PM sync: Decided to implement differential TTL resolution order: route override > tenant policy > global default. Also defined sampling presets for metrics to reduce snapshot size (full for logs/prompts, sampled for aggregated metrics).

2025-11-30 — Engineering update (Miguel Torres): Reconciler prototype completed for small tenants. Findings: S3 list operations are costly for large shards; switched to manifest-driven deletion list persisted during snapshot phase to avoid expensive listings.

2025-12-01 — Compliance review (Elena Rossi): Requested auditability SLA for reconciler runs and a manual trigger API for customers. Added follow-up to include signed attestation with verifier public key rotation details.
notes: Trade-offs: full snapshotting yields best forensic properties but increases storage and IO during purge windows. Mitigation: configurable sampling for aggregated metrics and incremental digest chaining to avoid re-hashing entire datasets. Rollout plan favors opt-in beta for high-compliance tenants before wide release.
